Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates bilateral, symmetric enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes with well-defined, lobulated margins and clear lung fields, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Stage I sarcoidosis. This pattern distinguishes it from malignancy (typically asymmetric/irregular), tuberculosis (often unilateral/calcified), or lymphoma (which usually presents with a mediastinal mass).
